A01.summary: Stated: V presents dialogue before a tactical scenario and after completion, before intermission. W menus list a Talk/persuade command with enemies. V guide records participant-specific persuasion/combat conditions. No script format, speaker/portrait table, dialogue line IDs, bark pool or full conversation graph was acquired; these are unread because no public internal corpus was located within this guide route.

yairpg.takeaway: Keep battle persuasion a current participant action with real consequences. A dramatic exchange is not proof of universal relationship mechanics.

A02.summary: Stated: V flow chart branches by protagonist and later route choices, rejoins numbered scenarios and lists optional SR objectives. Secret scenarios sit outside ordinary stage objectives. Script scheduling/journal recall and exact branching implementation remain unread; the guide is an authored route index, not source code.

yairpg.takeaway: Author route split, rejoin and optional outcomes separately. Maintain a causal receipt rather than infer which scenes were seen from stage number alone.

A03.summary: Unread: internal engine modules, scripting interpreter, event bus, data tables and main loop. Public guides show alternating phases and intermission but cannot establish code architecture. No executable/source package acquired, as this lane is public guides only and no install.

yairpg.takeaway: PROPOSAL: compare phase, story settlement and intermission as design boundaries; do not cite them as an inspected engine architecture.

A04.summary: Stated: W offers map-state Save and intermission Save Data. Its cleared-file guide specifies retained upgrades/money, sold parts and reset kill counts. V article mentions PS4/Vita cross-save. Binary format/versioning, autosave timing, migration, offline time and corruption/rejection handling remain unread. Titles and editions are kept separate.

yairpg.takeaway: Declare tactical resume, completed-arc carry and new-life start as separate persistence contracts. Preserve actor identity instead of turning each into prestige.

A05.summary: Stated: W End Phase passes control to the enemy. V flow objectives include retreat HP, movement-to-area and defeat triggers. These document scenario constraints, not an AI planner, targeting weights or off-screen NPC lives. Such algorithms are unread.

yairpg.takeaway: An enemy withdrawal threshold should create a visible tactical opportunity when observed. Do not invent a social AI model from a stage objective.

A06.summary: Stated in W menu reference: pilot, unit and weapon status are distinct; weapon view lists morale, energy/ammo, range, hit and terrain conditions. Intermission groups pilot training, unit upgrades, assignment, parts, shop and save. System settings include grid, animation toggles and shortcuts. This is guide-level UI evidence, not measured desktop behavior.

yairpg.takeaway: Show actor, equipment and action eligibility together on desktop. Name which resource blocks an attack; retain optional animation without hiding the receipt.

A07.summary: Unread: official author tools, script files, mod API, pack load order and validation. Akurasu authors maintain route and secret-condition tables, but wiki authoring does not establish game content authoring. No decompile or ROM acquisition.

yairpg.takeaway: Use a route-condition table as an original authoring proposal. It still needs a native consumer and validation before it is gameplay.

A08.summary: Stated: V objectives constrain turn counts, use of each attack, participant credit and retreat HP. Secrets add distinct character/group scores and prerequisite combinations. W exposes terrain, morale and resource costs. Full damage/hit formulas, RNG, seeds, difficulty curves, pity and economy scaling remain unread; no formula inferred from guide rows.

yairpg.takeaway: Record who earned each combat receipt and whether support credit qualifies. Optional mastery must not be a hidden universal morality score.

A09.summary: Stated: player/enemy phases and map turn limits drive optional objectives. W intermission follows battles; V routes use numbered scenarios and ordered participant checks. This is tactical/story progression, not a verified age calendar or offline system. Exact event priority when several triggers coincide is unread.

yairpg.takeaway: Use explicit deadline and settlement order for campaign events. Turn count and lived calendar time should not be merged without a world rule.

A10.summary: Stated: V has Beginner Mode and its opening SR objective asks use of all protagonist attacks; later objectives add coordinated kills/turn deadlines. Inferred: this can teach the action set through an optional goal. Full tutorial messages, unlock order and balancing are unread.

yairpg.takeaway: An optional opening objective can teach several useful verbs. Offer ordinary completion and explain known mastery terms without forcing perfect play.

A11.summary: Stated in W menu guide: battle animation/explosion can be toggled; grid and shortcuts can be configured; BGM can be assigned and protagonist weapons renamed. These are title-specific flavor and pacing controls. No accessibility audit or current platform parity proof.

yairpg.takeaway: Allow repeated-action feedback to be shortened while preserving outcomes. Cosmetic naming must not change action identity or save compatibility.

A12.summary: Stated: V has participant-specific secret recruitment/attacks, early-versus-late arrival, event-only survival, and unit upgrade transfers. W clear state trades parts for money and carries upgrades under its own rules. All-secret/series-wide catalogs, achievements and full DLC entitlement matrix remain unread.

yairpg.takeaway: Distinguish survival, recruitability, early arrival and playable control. A surviving NPC need not join the player's roster.
